subject.title: [Bug]: Daily-stale main heartbeat sends a greeting in the old session; user reply starts a disconnected new session

question: Should configured daily rollover take precedence over heartbeat session preservation, and should that be implemented through the proactive scheduler or a narrower heartbeat-specific lifecycle rule?
rationale: Current main deliberately protects system events from reset to prevent context loss, while the requested continuity requires rollover before a visible heartbeat; choosing the permanent precedence and upgrade behavior requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Use proactive daily rollover
options.body: Adapt and validate the scheduled-reset approach so stale main sessions roll before heartbeat or user traffic while active and provider-owned sessions remain protected.

options.title: Add heartbeat-specific rollover
options.body: Introduce a narrowly scoped rule for post-boundary main heartbeats, accepting additional complexity around determining whether the generated result will be visible.

options.title: Preserve current semantics
options.body: Keep all system events on the old session and document that a later user reply can begin a separate daily session.

recommendation.title: Use proactive daily rollover
recommendation.body: Adapt and validate the scheduled-reset approach so stale main sessions roll before heartbeat or user traffic while active and provider-owned sessions remain protected.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the daily reset contract and are the strongest documented owner for resolving its precedence against the later heartbeat-preservation behavior.
